henry.title: Dad's Trip: Distance and Time to Scotland
henry.intro: Dad is flying from Las Cruces to Scotland! Real facts: the trip is about 7,850 km in a straight line. 1 km is about 0.6 miles. A big plane flies about 800 km per hour. Scotland's clocks are 7 hours ahead of New Mexico this week. Use these facts and the Clock sim. (About 12 minutes.)
steps: FIRST (4 min): open the Clock sim and do the 3-step guide. You'll see two clocks, one for New Mexico and one for Scotland.
NEXT (7 min): answer worksheet questions 1 to 6. Use the facts above. Round numbers to make them easy (7,850 is about 8,000).
LAST: you're done when all 6 answers are written. Check: does each answer have a unit (miles, hours, days)?
links: Slide the clock and watch what time it is in Scotland.

steps: 1. Look at the two clocks. Tap 🏫 After school. Read both times.
2. Drag the slider. Watch the ☀️ turn into 🌙 and the words 'Next day!' appear in Scotland.
3. Tap Oct 25–31: 6 hours ahead. Scotland's clocks go back that weekend, so the gap gets smaller.
0.look: The sentence at the bottom tells you both times. Scotland time = New Mexico time + hours ahead.
0.q: Use the sim for questions 3, 4 and 5.

worksheet: A plane flies 800 km each hour. How many hours to fly 8,000 km? ___ hours
It is 3:30 PM after school in New Mexico. What time is it in Scotland? ___
Dad goes to bed at 10 PM in Scotland. What time is it in New Mexico? ___ Could you video-call him then? YES / NO
The sim's 'Oct 25–31' button: Scotland is ___ hours ahead.
Walking 5 km a day, about how many days would it take to walk 8,000 km? ___ days (hint: 8,000 ÷ 5)

frankie.title: Count Scotland! 🏰🐑
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: Dad is going on an airplane to Scotland! Let's count things that Scotland has: castles, sheep and tartan. (About 10 minutes.)
steps: Grown-up: point to each picture on the worksheet and count out loud together.
Frankie circles or draws the answers.
